statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk is 20% (watch) with NQ futures holding within roughly 15 points of the 30,906 session high inside a 0.74%-wide overnight band, while Stress of 55% (elevated) reflects long-end Treasury yields at two-decade highs against a live October Fed tightening debate.
recommendation: Tail remains in the WATCH band and below the block threshold. The concentrated whipsaw window is 12:15-14:45 UTC, spanning August durable goods orders at 12:30 UTC, the US cash open at 13:30 UTC and the final September Michigan sentiment reading at 14:00 UTC. Cleveland Fed President Hammack joins a policy panel at 18:00 UTC. US cash markets close at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures close for the week at 21:00 UTC, reopening at 22:00 UTC on Sunday.
headline: NQ holds just under a marginal new session high while flat long-end yields and an oil decline on Hormuz de-escalation keep Tail at the floor of WATCH
body:
NQ December futures trade near 30,890.75, up about 0.41%, roughly 15 points below the 30,905.75 session high inside an overnight band of 30,679.00-30,905.75. A second independent quote shows 30,894.00 with a 30,906.00 high, so both the level and the proximity to the extreme are corroborated. Price is therefore still holding near a session extreme, which is the single Tail amplifier genuinely present, and Tail stays in the WATCH band rather than returning to the low band.

Three observations keep it at the floor of that band. First, the extension is slight: over the past hour the session high advanced only about 15 points and the full band is 0.74% wide, so there is no sequence of failed retracements followed by fresh extension, which is the structure that actually overwhelms a mean-reversion book. Second, price has already backed off the extreme rather than defending it repeatedly. Third, the cross-asset stack is not aligned behind the move. Long-end yields are flat, not extending: the 10-year is 5.171% (+0.8bp) in a 5.163-5.189% range, the 2-year 4.899% (+0.4bp) and the 30-year 5.464% (+0.2bp), each within two to three basis points of the previous close even though the 30-year sits at its highest level since 2004 and the 10-year near levels last seen in 2007. WTI is 93.47 (-1.21%) and Brent 106.28 (-0.30%) after reports that the United States and Iran are discussing a phased agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and lift the naval blockade, so the energy channel is de-escalating rather than amplifying. VIX last closed at 15.67.

The cash index corroborates two-way behaviour: the Nasdaq-100 closed 24 September at 30,478.86, up only 0.03%, after ranging 30,204.16-30,529.35, which is an inside, mean-reverting session rather than a directional one. Breadth across indices is conflicting, with the Dow tracking a fourth consecutive losing week while the Nasdaq is up about 1.6% week to date; under this contract conflicting breadth reduces directional conviction and raises Stress rather than mechanically raising Tail.

Stress stays elevated at 55% on the macro regime rather than on index structure: the long end is at multi-decade highs, market-implied odds of an October rate increase are roughly 71-75%, and Brent has gained more than 17% during September amid the Iran conflict. That combination is a genuinely difficult environment that can still mean-revert, which is exactly the case where high Stress coexists with Tail below the block threshold.

Risk concentrates between 12:15 and 14:45 UTC, where August durable goods orders at 12:30 UTC, the US cash open at 13:30 UTC and the final September Michigan sentiment reading at 14:00 UTC fall in sequence. Durable goods consensus is near -0.3% against a prior 1.1%; the release has not printed at the time of this assessment, so it raises Stress and lowers Confidence rather than Tail. Escalation above the block threshold would require observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements, together with the yield, volatility and energy channels turning aligned.

Confidence is 87% on two corroborated real-time NQ quotes, real-time 2-year, 10-year and 30-year yields, current oil prices with session changes and a verified event calendar. The shared Finviz context file was read and found stale and partial, with a collection timestamp of 2026-09-25T01:58:09Z and its calendar and futures sections unavailable, so it was excluded from this assessment and independent research was used throughout. VIX is a previous-close value because US cash markets are shut.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 published Claude assessments held Tail between 17% and 25%, touching the block threshold once at 09:00 UTC on 24 September during a trend-down European morning before decaying through the US session. Stress stayed elevated in a 52-59% band throughout, reflecting the ongoing long-end repricing, and Confidence held between 85% and 88%. From 17:00 UTC the sequence settled into the low Tail band, with the mode shifting from mixed to normal after 01:00 UTC as the overnight path narrowed, then turning to trend-up at 06:00 UTC as NQ cleared its earlier overnight high.
outlookSummary: The base case is two-way rotation around the session high through the European morning, with Tail holding at the floor of WATCH on gap and headline exposure rather than observed structure, and a small lift at 09:00 UTC where liquidity peaks. Risk concentrates between 12:15 and 14:45 UTC, where August durable goods orders, the US cash open and the final Michigan sentiment reading fall in sequence into a market pricing roughly 71-75% odds of an October rate increase; the mode is expected to turn event/whipsaw there, with Tail peaking at 24% and remaining inside WATCH. Escalation above the block threshold would require observed opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements. The afternoon carries a further checkpoint at 18:00 UTC with Fed Hammack's policy panel remarks and a power hour into the 20:00 UTC cash close. US cash markets close at 20:00 UTC and CME equity index futures close for the week at 21:00 UTC, so the final ten slots of the horizon fall inside the weekend halt, where no tradable price path exists; those hours publish residual Tail near 5-7% with Confidence decaying as the last observed structure ages.
